title: ModernEdge Activation & Ops Handoff
summary: Kickoff for ModernEdge activation and operational handoff. Reviewed networking/VPC options, authentication (SAML/SSO), data residency, and pilot success criteria. Went over runbook, staging access, and a short checklist for first-week tasks. Decided to start with a small hosted pilot with dedicated VPC peering and plan for Dedicated capacity after benchmarks.
next_steps: Redwood to share staging runbook and API access playbook by 2026-07-13
Customer to provide firewall and VPC CIDR details by 2026-07-14
Schedule performance benchmark slot (30m) w/ SE for week of 2026-07-20
action_items: Samir Patel: Share staging runbook and onboarding deck - due 2026-07-13
Marcus Reed: Send VPC/CIDR + proxy info - due 2026-07-14
Elena Morris: Book benchmark session and prepare load profile spreadsheet - due 2026-07-17
Priya Nair: Confirm encryption/KMS requirements and regulatory check list - due 2026-07-16
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-11 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Elena (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood CSM), Karen (ModernEdge CTO), Marcus (Eng Lead), Priya (InfoSec), Diego (DevOps)

Auto-summary (auto): Quick kickoff and handoff for activation. Some audio dropouts around 00:22.

[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick us off. Quick intros — I'm Samir, AE; Elena's our solutions engineer, Ravi is your CSM. ModernEdge, welcome — maybe quick intros?
[00:14] Karen Liu: Hi, Karen here, CTO at ModernEdge. We're excited to get the inference rollout started for our support automation and code-assist features.
[00:22] Marcus Reed: Marcus, engineering lead, will run the integration team. Sorry if I cut out a little there, wifi's a bit meh.
[00:28] Priya Nair: Priya from InfoSec - I'll be the point on compliance and keys.
[00:33] Diego Alvarez: Diego, ops - I'll handle VPC and networking.
[00:37] Samir Patel: Great — agenda is short: access/runbook, network/VPC options, SSO and RBAC, pilot scope & SLOs, then next steps.
[00:47] Elena Morris: I'll cover the staging traffic and benchmark plan after the network bits — also quick note on telemetry and the Console dashboards you'll see.
[00:55] Diego Alvarez: On VPC — we prefer a VPC peering model rather than full on-prem, we use AWS Account scoping, and a transit gateway; we need to understand if Redwood supports peering + security groups one-way.
[01:05] Elena Morris: Yes, we do. Option A is simple peering into Redwood Private endpoint with short-lived certs, Option B is customer-managed VPN. Most customers start with peering for latency. We'll send a runbook.
[01:17] Priya Nair: For keys — we need to know if KMS is customer-managed, and do you support HSM backends? Also SOC 2 scope and audit logs retention.
[01:28] Ravi Choudhary: We support customer KMS integration; HSM-backed KMS can be used via your cloud KMS provider. Audit logs are stored in the control plane and can be exported to your SIEM; retention is configurable. I'll attach the security pack.
[01:40] Karen Liu: Good. Data residency — pilot data must stay in us-east-1 region.
[01:45] Samir Patel: Noted. We'll pin the pilot to us-east-1.
[01:48] Marcus Reed: On capacity — we plan to start with low traffic, 10 QPS average, bursty during day peaks. What's the recommended starting footprint?
[01:56] Elena Morris: For that profile, a small Dedicated pool or Hosted with reserved concurrency could work. Dedicated gives you predictable latency SLAs; hosted is faster to stand up. Many teams kick off with hosted + VPC peering, then move to Dedicated once benchmarks justify it.
[02:12] Marcus Reed: Latency vs cost — do you have typical per-token latency expectations on short prompts?
[02:18] Elena Morris: For 8k context with batching off, sub-120ms p95 per token is achievable on our verified Llama-X quantized profile in hosted. But it depends on prompt shape — we'll run a short benchmark.
[02:30] Diego Alvarez: Can you run benchmarks behind our NAT? We can't open public endpoints.
[02:34] Elena Morris: Yes — either peered subnet or private endpoint. We can bring a load runner into your VPC for the benchmark.
[02:40] Priya Nair: Also want to confirm logging of token payloads, we need redaction.
[02:44] Ravi Choudhary: Redwood has configurable telemetry. Payload retention can be turned off and we support token-level redaction and differential logging for PHI. We'll include the config snippets.
[02:55] Karen Liu: Timeline — we want a pilot running by end of next week. Is that realistic?
[03:00] Samir Patel: Realistic if we lock down network and provide access credentials by mid-week. We'll need about 3 items from you: VPC CIDRs, a test service account/role for the benchmark runner, and SAML metadata for SSO.
[03:10] Marcus Reed: We'll get CIDRs and a test role. SAML — we want to integrate with Okta and have SSO for the Console.
[03:16] Elena Morris: Okta is supported. We map SAML attributes to RBAC roles. We'll send the RBAC mapping template.
[03:23] Diego Alvarez: On observability — does the Console expose per-route token cost breakout? We'd like early visibility.
[03:29] Ravi Choudhary: Yes, Console shows token-level cost, latency histograms, per-run logs; we can provision a read-only role for your finance/ops users.
[03:38] Priya Nair: Compliance — do you provide a SOC 2 attestation and data processing addendum?
[03:42] Samir Patel: Yes, standard DPA and SOC 2 Type II reports are available. We'll share links to the compliance pack in the follow-up.
[03:48] Marcus Reed: A few technical Qs — model pinning, can we pin model versions for the pilot to avoid unexpected regressions?
[03:54] Elena Morris: Absolutely. You can pin by model and version in the route config and set auto-fallback to a compatible quantized variant. We also have eval hooks if you want to run a small regression test on deploys.
[04:06] Karen Liu: For the runbook handoff — can you walk through week-1 checklist?
[04:11] Ravi Choudhary: Sure — week 0: networking + SSO, week 1: staging access and smoke tests, week 2: benchmark and load test, week 3: canary to production routes. We'll email the week-by-week runbook.
[04:26] Elena Morris: I'll highlight the benchmark plan: we'll need a sample prompt corpus, target QPS, and preferred latency SLOs. We'll run both throughput and tail-latency tests.
[04:36] Marcus Reed: About prompt corpus — we'll share 300 representative queries from support agents and 100 dev queries for code-assist.
[04:43] Elena Morris: Perfect. If you can mark which contain PII, we'll configure redaction.
[04:48] Diego Alvarez: Small question on caching — do you have prefix caching or KV cache options? We use a lot of few-shot prompts that could benefit.
[04:55] Elena Morris: We have prefix/KV caching and configurable TTLs; caching can dramatically reduce token cost for repeated prefixes, but we recommend validating correctness for any stateful prompts.
[05:05] Karen Liu: Security checklist: KMS integration, access logs to SIEM, SSO, and encrypted in-flight. Anything else?
[05:12] Priya Nair: Also need role-based access for engineers vs product.
[05:15] Samir Patel: We'll provide a sample RBAC mapping for Okta groups, and a security pack with KMS and audit export details.
[05:22] Marcus Reed: Are there any gotchas with on-prem/private? We're thinking of a later phase where some models may run on our data center.
[05:29] Elena Morris: For on-prem, we provide a private deployment package, but network latency and GPU procurement are the typical blockers. For your timeline I'd recommend starting hosted with VPC peering and then evaluate private/Dedicated after the benchmark.
[05:43] Diego Alvarez: Understood. One more ops detail — who owns model updates? Will updates be rolled automatically?
[05:48] Ravi Choudhary: Model rollouts are controlled by you. We support canary and A/B rollouts, and automatic rollback on regression alerts if enabled.
[05:56] Elena Morris: I'll also send a quick checklist for telemetry keys and the Console readouts you'll see during the benchmark.
[06:03] Karen Liu: Great. Anything else on timeline?
[06:07] Samir Patel: Recap: Redwood to share runbook + security pack + RBAC template by Tue 2026-07-13. Customer to share VPC details, test role, and Okta metadata by Thu 2026-07-14. SE team to run benchmark week of 2026-07-20.
[06:23] Marcus Reed: Sounds good. We'll try to expedite the VPC details.
[06:26] Priya Nair: I'll review the security pack as soon as it's up.
[06:29] Samir Patel: Ok closing notes — attaching the shared artifacts: onboarding deck (link: https://redwood.app/decks/modernedge-onboard), staging runbook (link: https://redwood.app/runbooks/modernedge-staging), security pack (link: https://redwood.app/security/pack).
[06:44] Diego Alvarez: Small audio blip — Diego sorry, I missed the link for the runbook?
[06:48] Samir Patel: Runbook is in chat and I'll email it along with the security DPA.
[06:52] Karen Liu: Thanks everyone, excited to get started.
[06:55] Samir Patel: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the artifacts and next steps.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription: occasional stutters and a ~6s dropout at ~00:22, speaker overlaps around 04:40. Some proper nouns mistranscribed (Infrakit heard as infra-kit).
